results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) completes Rp 6.54 trillion shareholder loan from PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) to PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC)
results.body: The article reports that PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) facilitated a shareholder loan (SHL) of Rp 6.54 trillion between its subsidiaries PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) and PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC) on 17 September 2026. JSMR holds 65% of JTT and JTT holds 40% of JJC, and the loan is intended to bridge JJC’s refinancing and other operational needs with an interest rate within the market range. The transaction reduces JSMR’s cash and cash equivalents by roughly Rp 6.54 trillion and increases other receivables by the same amount, while its total liabilities were about Rp 100 trillion as of June 2026; the loan has no immediate impact on revenue or expenses, and JSMR’s first‑half 2026 toll revenue rose 6.8% to Rp 9.5 trillion, net profit about Rp 1.9 trillion and EBITDA grew about 8%. Panin Sekuritas analyst Elandry Pratama recommends a “buy on weakness” for JSMR with a target price of Rp 3,800–4,000 per share, noting the loan supports JJC’s liquidity while increasing intra‑group funding exposure.

results.title: Ahead of Haji Isam’s entry into PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN), director Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod sells shares worth Rp2.47 billion
results.body: Director Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod of PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) sold 185,200 shares at Rp13,352 each, totaling about Rp2.47 billion, reducing his holding to 3,8148 million shares (0.01% voting rights). The sale was reported to OJK on 22 Sep 2026, and BYAN’s share price fell 9.71% (1,275 points) to Rp11,850 on that day, though the stock remains up 16.18% week‑to‑date and 7.73% over three months with a market cap of roughly Rp400 trillion. Meanwhile, PT Jhonlin Baratama, a subsidiary of the Jhonlin Group owned by Haji Isam, signed a conditional share purchase agreement to acquire 10,000,000,500 BYAN shares (about 30% of the total 33.33 billion) pending conditions, following prior agreements by major shareholders Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low who together hold 62.25% of BYAN.

results.title: Bayan Resources (BYAN) CFO Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod sells 185,200 shares as H Isam’s 30% stake acquisition proceeds
results.body: Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod, director and Chief Financial Officer of Bayan Resources (BYAN), sold 185,200 shares on 21 September 2026. The shares were sold at Rp13,352 per share, generating approximately Rp2.47 billion and reducing his holding to 3,814 million shares (0.01% of BYAN). The divestment coincides with the finalisation of a conditional sale agreement signed on 16 September 2026, under which Jhonlin Baratama, part of Jhonlin Group led by H Isam, will acquire 10,000,000,500 shares representing a 30 % stake in Bayan Resources. Following the acquisition, Bayan Resources received an additional coal production quota of up to 20 million tonnes for its subsidiaries Tiwa Abadi (TA), Tanur Jaya (TJ) and Fajar Sakti Prima (FSP), as approved by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources.

results.title: PT Victoria Investama Tbk (VICO) approves cash dividend of Rp8 per share for FY 2025
results.body: PT Victoria Investama Tbk (VICO) approved at its extraordinary general meeting on 18 September 2026 a cash dividend for the 2025 financial year of Rp8 per share, totaling Rp121,736,605,264. The dividend will be payable to shareholders of record on 30 September 2026, with payment scheduled for 22 October 2026, following cum-dividend and ex-dividend dates set between 28 September and 1 October 2026.

results.title: Analyst highlights nickel stock recommendations and sector outlook amid RKAB and HPM regulatory pressure
results.body: David Kurniawan of PT Indo Premier Sekuritas says nickel issuers remain under pressure in 2026 because of global oversupply, uncertainty over RKAB approval and new HPM regulations. Year‑to‑date, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) fell 9.57%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) dropped 18.67%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) slid 11.3%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) declined 8.97%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) plunged 64.61%, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) posted a modest 0.63% gain. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as ANTM and INCO have stronger resilience due to diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. He expects the sector’s outlook to improve gradually in 2027 if RKAB approvals proceed smoothly and cost‑efficiency measures take effect.

results.title: PT Fast Food Indonesia Tbk (FAST) to Hold Extraordinary General Meeting on 14 October 2026 to Approve Board Changes and Articles Amendment
results.body: PT Fast Food Indonesia Tbk (FAST) will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) on 14 October 2026. The agenda seeks shareholder approval for changes to the board of directors and an amendment to the articles of association, specifically Article 3 on the company's purpose, objectives and business activities, to align with the 2025 Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification (KBLI). The meeting will be conducted in a hybrid format via eASY.KSEI and physically at the Gelael building, with voting rights limited to shareholders recorded in the KSEI list as of 21 September 2026 who hold written confirmation or a proxy. FAST reported a net loss attributable to its parent entities of Rp56.74 billion for the first half of 2026, a sharp decline from the Rp138.75 billion loss in the same period of the prior year.

results.title: PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS) and PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) held extraordinary general meetings on 22 September 2026, with DMAS shares falling 3.7% and SILO shares gaining 0.97%.
results.body: On 22 September 2026 PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS) and PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) conducted extraordinary general meetings (RUPSLB) to approve corporate actions. DMAS approved the resignation of director Atsushi Uehara and the appointment of Shinji Yoneda as Vice President Director, and its shares closed 3.70% lower at IDR 182 after opening at IDR 189, while the company reported marketing sales of IDR 1.15 trillion (55% of its annual target) and net profit of about IDR 1.19 trillion. SILO secured shareholder approval to acquire a portfolio of 14 hospitals from First REIT valued at IDR 6.91 trillion, obtained asset guarantees exceeding 50% of equity for a syndicated loan facility up to IDR 14.5 trillion, and its shares closed 0.97% higher at IDR 2,080, touching an intraday high of IDR 2,090. Mirae Asset Sekuritas and Korea Investment & Sekuritas Indonesia (KISI) recommended buying DMAS with a target price of IDR 260, while MNC Sekuritas recommended buying SILO with a target price of IDR 2,750, noting the acquisition’s potential to expand SILO’s asset base but also raising concerns about leverage and post‑acquisition ROIC.

results.title: PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) shares jump 9.94% as Gabriel Rey and Andry Hakim acquire 20% stake
results.body: PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) shares surged 9.94% to close at Rp1,715 on Tuesday (22 Sep 2026), after rising 45.34% in the week and 114.38% in the month, following Gabriel Rey (through PT Pukul Rata Kanan) and Andry Hakim (through PT Hakimson Growth Capital) buying a combined 20% stake from PT Catur Dharma Anugerah Surya. PT Pukul Rata Kanan purchased 65.25 million shares at Rp428 each (≈Rp27.93 billion) and PT Hakimson Growth Capital bought 21.75 million shares at the same price (≈Rp9.31 billion), for a total transaction value of about Rp37.24 billion. The price rise gives the investors potential capital gains of roughly Rp83.98 billion for Gabriel Rey and Rp27.99 billion for Andry Hakim, totaling nearly Rp112 billion, and the stock touched the Auto Reject Top (ARA) level. In the first half of 2026, TRUK reported revenue of Rp19.24 billion, down from Rp19.62 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of Rp3.76 billion, widening from Rp3.13 billion in H1 2025.

results.title: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) announces interim dividend payment schedule for FY 2026
results.body: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) disclosed that it will distribute a cash interim dividend for the 2026 fiscal year. The dividend totals US$10 million, equivalent to approximately Rp 1.42 per share, and was approved by the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners on 18 September 2026. Key dates are: cum‑dividend on the regular and negotiation markets on 30 September 2026, ex‑dividend on 1 October 2026; for the cash market, cum‑dividend on 2 October 2026, ex‑dividend on 5 October 2026, with the recording date set for 2 October 2026 at 16:00 and payment scheduled for 22 October 2026. For the six‑month period ending 30 June 2026, the company reported net profit attributable to its parent of US$17.29 million, retained earnings of US$98.90 million and total equity of US$1.11 billion, while its shares closed at Rp 620, down 2.36 % on 22 September 2026.

results.title: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) to distribute US$10 million interim dividend as its shares fall 63,85% year-to-date
results.body: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA), 60% owned by PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) and 30% by Phoenix Power BV, announced a US$10 million interim cash dividend of Rp1,422181 per share, with a cum-dividend date of 30 September 2026 and payment on 22 October 2026. The dividend comes as CDIA’s share price closed at Rp 620 on 22 September 2026, down 2.36% on the day and 63.85% year-to-date.

results.title: Technical stock recommendations for PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII), and PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) on 23/9/2026
results.body: On 23/9/2026 the report offers technical recommendations for PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) and PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) following the IHSG close at 6,277.04, down 1.69%. DSSA closed at Rp 980, down 4.39%, with a Trading Buy recommendation, support at Rp 920 and resistance at Rp 1,115 amid a three‑black‑crows pattern, weakening RSI and rising volume. ASII closed at Rp 4,780, down 0.83%, and is advised to Hold with support at Rp 4,720 and resistance at Rp 4,990 as bearish consolidation and negative RSI signals persist. TOWR closed at Rp 404, down 2.42%, and is suggested as Buy on Weakness with support around Rp 386‑394, resistance at Rp 430 and a potential breakdown support at Rp 380 as RSI approaches oversold.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily bought ten stocks as the IHSG fell 1.68% to 6,277 on Tuesday (22/9)
results.body: Foreign investors recorded net purchases in ten Indonesian listed companies while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.68% (107 points) to 6,277.04 on Tuesday (22/9/2026). The session saw 33.71 billion shares traded, valued at Rp14.52 trillion, and foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp131.72 billion across the market, with 533 stocks closing weaker, 139 stronger and 118 stagnant. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net buying were PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) Rp36.89 billion, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) Rp30.33 billion, PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) Rp27.60 billion, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) Rp25.24 billion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) Rp24.12 billion, PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) Rp22.41 billion, PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) Rp21.74 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp19.95 billion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) Rp19.02 billion and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) Rp17.33 billion. These net purchases occurred despite the broader market correction.

results.title: PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS) Approves Appointment of New Vice President Director
results.body: PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS) held an extraordinary general meeting on 22 September 2026 that approved changes to its board of directors. Atsushi Uehara resigned as Vice President Director and was replaced by Shinji Yoneda, who was appointed as the new Vice President Director. Following the changes, the board now consists of Hongky Jeffry Nantung as President Director, Shinji Yoneda as Vice President Director, and Monik William and Tondy Suwanto as Directors.

results.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) secures approval for its 2026 RKAB, raising the production quota to ~23 Mt and prompting buy recommendations
results.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) has received government approval for its revised 2026 Work Plan and Budget (RKAB), increasing the coal production quota to roughly 23 million tonnes. In the first half of 2026 the company reported revenue of about US$1 billion, up 9% YoY, and net profit attributable to shareholders of US$106 million, up 16% YoY, while production was 9.9 million tonnes, down 5% YoY but Q2 output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tonnes. UBS Sekuritas and KB Valbury Sekuritas upgraded their outlook, issuing buy recommendations with target prices of Rp 30,000 and Rp 29,300 per share respectively, whereas Mirae Asset Sekuritas advised a wait‑and‑see stance. The firm faces risks from higher mining and transport costs, logistics constraints and possible tighter quota approvals for 2027‑2028, while its renewable‑energy portfolio grew to 86 MWp of operating solar capacity, supporting its long‑term diversification strategy.

results.title: PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) director Alastair Gordon Christopher Mcleod sells 185,200 shares at Rp 13,352 each ahead of Haji Isam’s planned acquisition
results.body: PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) director Alastair Gordon Christopher Mcleod sold 185,200 shares at Rp 13,352 each on 21 September 2026, following the announcement of a share purchase transaction with Jhonlin Group. The sale generated a profit of about Rp 2.47 billion and reduced his holding to roughly 3.81 million shares (0.01% of BYAN). At the close of trading on 22 September, BYAN shares were at Rp 11,850, down 9.71% for the day, while a conditional share purchase agreement signed on 16 September targets the Low family’s roughly 62% stake in BYAN for acquisition by PT Jhonlin Baratama, which would become the new controller. The proposed US$3 billion (≈Rp 52.6 trillion) offer reflects an estimated 80% discount to BYAN’s market capitalization of about US$26 billion.

results.title: Profit Grows for Multiple Regional Development Banks Despite Credit Contraction
results.body: Profit rose across a number of regional development banks (BPDs) in August 2026 despite declines in credit portfolios, with PT Bank Pembangunan Daerah Jawa Barat dan Banten Tbk (BJBR) posting a 58.7% YoY increase in net profit to Rp923.26 billion while its credit fell 3.7% YoY. Similar patterns were observed at Bank BPD DIY, Bank Jatim (BJTM), Bank Banten (BEKS), Bank Sumsel Babel, Bank Jakarta and Bank Nagari, where net profit growth ranged from about 2% to 284% and fee‑based income rose, offsetting modest credit contractions or, in the case of Bank Banten, strong credit expansion.

results.title: Energy Minister Bahlil Plans to Streamline Tender Process for Indonesia's 100 GW Solar Power Project
results.body: Indonesia’s Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia announced plans to streamline the tender process for the nation’s 100 GW solar power program, aiming to reduce bureaucracy and accelerate project execution. He estimated the project will require US$70‑73 billion in investment and emphasized a win‑win approach, prioritising domestic manufacturing while allowing selective imports when necessary. The government has already launched about 5.5 GW in the first phase and expects to add 25‑30 GW of solar capacity this year, with President Prabowo Subianto having inaugurated the program in August. State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi also set a target of 30 GW of solar capacity and the retirement of 13 GW of diesel power plants by the end of the year.

results.title: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) to distribute USD10 million interim dividend, schedule announced
results.body: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) announced an interim cash dividend of USD10 million for FY 2026, equivalent to Rp1,422,181 per share. The dividend, approved by the board and commissioners on 18 September 2026, will be payable on 22 October 2026, with cum‑dividend dates on 30 September (regular market) and 2 October (cash market) and ex‑dividend dates on 1 October and 5 October respectively. CDIA reported net profit attributable to the parent of USD17,287 million, retained earnings of USD98,899 million, and total equity of USD1,107 billion as of 30 June 2026. CDIA is a subsidiary of PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) of the Barito Group owned by Prajogo Pangestu and partners with EGCO Group (Electricity Generating Public Company Limited) of Thailand.

results.title: PT Alam Sutera Realty Tbk (ASRI) to launch eight premium Agna units by year‑end as H1 2026 net profit falls 69%
results.body: PT Alam Sutera Realty Tbk (ASRI) announced that it will market eight units of the new premium Agna type in the The Gramercy cluster by the end of 2026, priced at Rp28.86 billion each. The Agna units feature high‑end specifications such as imported marble flooring, smart‑home systems, private lifts and private pools, and the development’s Grand Clubhouse is slated to open in October 2026. The company said its sales strategy remains focused on exclusivity, targeting two to three premium units per month and avoiding mass‑market volume. Despite the product push, ASRI reported a 69.34% decline in net profit to Rp12.7 billion for the first semester of 2026, while revenue grew 18.3% year‑on‑year to Rp1.3 trillion.

results.title: EURO shareholders approve up to 2 billion new shares in rights issue and appoint former commissioner as director
results.body: On 18 September 2026, EURO held an extraordinary shareholders meeting that approved a rights issue of up to 2 billion new shares at a nominal price of Rp5 per share, representing 78.47% of the current share capital. The company said the fresh capital will be used for working capital and to expand its production capacity. The meeting also removed Commissioner Darren Nathaniel Tandra, appointed him as a director until 2 June 2031, and named Dionisius Indri Priyobodo as the new commissioner. The revised board now includes Sumadi Rusli as chairman commissioner, Dionisius Indri Priyobodo as commissioner, and directors Marianti Hidayat (President Director), Suryati and Darren Nathaniel Tandra.

results.title: Drs. Hendro Martowardojo Buy Shares of Resource Alam Indonesia
results.body: Insider Drs. Hendro Martowardojo purchased 93,000 shares of Resource Alam Indonesia at IDR 328 per share, costing IDR 30,504,000, raising his stake to 5,807,528 shares (0.116%) from 0.114%. The transaction follows earlier buys of 300,000 shares on Aug 27 at IDR 288 and 200,000 shares on Sep 17 at IDR 309.853, reflecting a continued accumulation that has increased his holding by roughly 593,000 shares over the past six weeks.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) raises 2026 capex and maintains oil and gas production guidance
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) increased its 2026 capital expenditure target to USD450-475 million for oil and gas and up to USD50 million for electricity while keeping its oil‑gas production guidance at 165-170 mboepd and targeting 4,550 GWh of electricity sales. In the first half of 2026 the company reported net profit attributable to the parent of USD275 million on revenue of USD1,415 billion, EBITDA of USD805 million and gross profit of USD588 million, with production reaching 170 mboepd (72% gas) and cash cost below USD10 per boe, supported by projects such as Sakakemang (first gas expected Q3 2027) and full‑scale operation of Senoro Phase 2A since June 2026.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) completes a IDR 6.54 trillion shareholder loan and is recommended as a buy
results.body: On 17 September 2026, PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) facilitated a IDR 6.54 trillion shareholder loan from its 65%-owned subsidiary PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) to JTT’s 40%-owned subsidiary PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC), reducing JSMR’s cash and cash equivalents by the same amount while leaving its revenue and expenses unchanged. Panin Sekuritas Pondok Indah analyst Elandry Pratama projects continued toll‑traffic growth, noting H1 2026 revenue of IDR 9.5 trillion (+6.8%) and net profit of IDR 1.9 trillion, and recommends a buy on weakness with a target price of IDR 3,800‑4,000 per share despite JSMR’s IDR 100 trillion liabilities.

results.title: Assessing Danantara’s issuer prospects amid the Bursa Efek Indonesia demutualization
results.body: The article examines the outlook for PT Danantara Investment Management (DIM) as it prepares to acquire an estimated 40.12% stake in Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) following the demutualization mandated by POJK No. 13/2026. Fitch Ratings maintains DIM’s long‑term foreign and local‑currency issuer rating at BBB with a negative outlook, noting that the rating reflects Indonesia’s sovereign risk rather than a deterioration of BUMN quality, and cites a 2025 capital injection of Rp 70 trillion from BPI Danantara sourced through PT Danantara Asset Management (DAM). Analysts warn that Danantara’s potential shareholding above the 5% threshold could raise governance and conflict‑of‑interest concerns for BUMN issuers, although the demutualization does not directly alter their fundamentals. The commentary recommends buying several BUMN stocks, citing target prices of Rp 4,000 for BBRI, Rp 5,400 for BMRI, Rp 3,400 for TLKM (Rully) and Rp 3,450 for TLKM (Kevin), Rp 3,800 for JSMR, and Rp 4,100 for ANTM. Overall, while DIM’s rating and capital base remain solid, investors are advised to monitor governance risks and policy independence as Danantara’s BEI stake materializes.

results.title: Factors Driving PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) Net Profit Surge 796% YoY
results.body: The article explains the drivers behind PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC)’s net profit surge of 796.52% YoY to US$275.32 million in the first half of 2026. The jump results from a 23.35% revenue increase to US$1.41 billion, a 30.17% rise in gross profit to US$588.5 million, and a US$124.11 million contribution from associate PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) (US$104.17 million), joint‑venture PT Transportasi Gas Indonesia (TGI) (US$17.16 million) and affiliated PT Api Metra Graha (AMG) (US$2.10 million), while cost of goods sold grew only 18.92% as exploration expenses fell 73.06% and electricity‑sales costs dropped 15.33%. Consequently, Medco’s net profit margin rose to 19.46% from 2.68% in H1 2025, with the sharp YoY growth also reflecting the low profit base of US$100.92 million in H1 2025 after a 72.53% decline from 2024.

results.title: PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) Secures Rp14.5 Trillion Syndicated Loan to Finance Acquisition of 14 Hospitals
results.body: On 22 September 2026, PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) secured a syndicated loan facility of Rp14.5 trillion to fund its acquisition of 14 hospital operators from First Real Estate Investment Trust. The loan is provided by a consortium of banks—BNI, Bank CIMB Niaga, BCA, Bank DBS Indonesia, MUFG Bank and HSBC—and shareholders have pledged guarantees on the acquired hospital assets. The transaction is valued at approximately Rp6.91 trillion, split into a first tranche of Rp4.08 trillion for eight targets and a second tranche of Rp2.83 trillion for six targets, representing about 67.57 % of Siloam’s equity of Rp10.23 trillion as of 31 March 2026. The directly impacted targets are PT Sriwijaya Mega Abadi (SMA), PT Eka Dasa Parinama (EDP), PT Sentra Dinamika Perkasa (SDP), PT Graha Indah Pratama (GIP), PT Dasa Graha Jaya (DGJ), PT Nusa Bahana Niaga (NBN) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Buton Bangun Cipta (BBC) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Menara Abadi Megah (MAM) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Prima Labuan Bajo (PLB), PT Perisai Dunia Sejahtera (PDS), PT Bayutama Sukses (BS), PT Primatama Cemerlang (PC), PT Graha Pilar Sejahtera (GPS) and PT Yogya Central Terpadu (YCT) Divisi Rumah Sakit, which will become subsidiaries of Siloam.

results.title: IHSG slides 1.69% to 6,277; analysts' stock picks for Wednesday (23/9)
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.69% (107.68 points) to 6,277.04 on Tuesday, prompting analysts to highlight select stocks for Wednesday trading. PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) closed down 4.39% at Rp 980, with support at Rp 920 and resistance at Rp 1,115, and analysts recommended a buy on a technical rebound. PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) slipped 2.42% to Rp 404, with support around Rp 386–Rp 394 and a target resistance of Rp 430, suggesting a buy‑on‑weakness strategy if price holds above support. PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) declined 0.83% to Rp 4,780, with support at Rp 4,720 and resistance at Rp 4,990, and analysts advised holding pending confirmation of momentum improvement.

results.title: Stock Moves of Salim to Prajogo Conglomerate Issuers: Who Delivered the Highest Returns?
results.body: The article reviews the year‑to‑date (YTD) share‑price performance of issuers affiliated with Salim Group, Astra Group and Prajogo Pangestu group in 2026. Salim affiliates PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) surged 36.82% to Rp1,635, reporting 16% revenue growth to Rp2.69 trillion and a 25% net‑profit rise to Rp891 billion, while PT Salim Ivomas Pratama Tbk (SIMP) and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) posted gains of 7.89% to Rp615 and 3.32% to Rp7,000 respectively. Astra affiliates PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) climbed 25.28% to Rp3,370 with revenue up 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion and net profit up 22.6% to about Rp1.15 trillion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) rose 13.22% to Rp8,350, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) fell 16.27% to Rp24,700. Prajogo Pangestu affiliates PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) dropped 50.57% to Rp5,400 despite a 59.56% revenue jump to US$543.98 million, and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) also slumped sharply, underscoring weaker YTD returns for the Prajogo group.

results.title: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) Announces US$10 million Interim Dividend for FY 2026
results.body: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA), owned by the Prajogo Pangestu conglomerate, announced an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026. The dividend is set at Rp1.42 per share, amounting to a total of US$10 million, with a recording date of 2 October 2026 and cum‑ex dates of 30 September/1 October for the regular market and 2 October/5 October for the cash market. For the half‑year ended 30 June 2026, the company reported net profit of US$17.28 million, while H1 2026 results showed revenue of US$82.1 million (up 22.8% YoY), EBITDA of US$31.6 million (up 25.3% YoY) and an EBITDA margin improvement to 38.5% from 37.7%. Logistics revenue surged 80.2% YoY to US$27 million, energy revenue rose 5.4% YoY to US$51.8 million, and gross profit increased 2.8% YoY to US$19.6 million.

results.title: Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara says Rp218.3 trillion BLBI bond repayment completed; government retains claim on obligors
results.body: Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara announced that the government has fully repaid the Rp218.3 trillion of BLBI‑related government bonds issued to address the 1997‑1998 crisis. The final payment was made on 24 August using non‑tax state revenue derived from a Bank Indonesia surplus, and the repayment does not affect the state’s right to claim outstanding obligations from BLBI obligors and debtors. Collection will continue under the Ministry of Finance’s Directorate General of State Assets and the National Debt Committee, guided by PP No. 4/2026, after the BLBI task force concluded at the end of 2024.
